newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela blames Placer Dome for gold mine delay.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela blames Placer Dome for gold mine delay.

text.p: Venezuelan state-owned industrial holding Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) blamed Canadian mining company Placer Dome on Friday for delays in a planned $576 million gold mine project.
CVG, which has a 30 percent stake in the project, said Placer planned to use the Las Cristinas gold beds in the southwestern Venezuelan state of Bolivar as collateral against project financing.
"But the beds are Venezuelan property", CVG said in a statement, and instead, "Placer should use plant and installations" to back the loans.
"That is all that is holding back the project," the CVG added.
Placer meanwhile said in a separate statement that it was merely waiting for CVG to agree shareholder contracts so construction could go ahead, as first planned for December.
"We want to continue work...but, unfortunately, this is not something that depends exclusively on us," Placer said.
CVG said it had complied with all requirements -- including agreements on the provision of electricity -- and that "the project would continue to count on CVG's support."
